newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - FOCUS REMAINS ON TREASURIES.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - FOCUS REMAINS ON TREASURIES.

text.p: Trading of U.S. corporate bonds was extremely thin on Wednesday with market players focusing mostly on a rebounding Treasury market, traders said.
"The market caught a little bit of summer dolldrums," said one high-grade corporate bond trader. "On a day like today, corporates took a back seat to Treasuries."
Spreads on investment-grade corporates and prices of junk bonds ended the day mostly unchanged, traders reported.
Recovering from yesterday's sell-off, Treasury prices rebounded in reaction to benign retail sales and producer price data for July.
After dropping 13/32 on Tuesday, the price of the 30-year benchmark Treasury rose 20/32, closing at a price of 96-25/32 on Wednesday.
In the junk bond market, some dealers were reducing their positions as they prepared to leave for vacation.
"We saw some volume in telecom paper as dealers lightened up on positions," one trader said. "People who are willing to sell have had no problem finding buyers," he noted.
Among individual credits, Speedy Muffler King 10 7/8 percent notes due '06 dropped 3.5 points to 94-95 as the company's earnings came in below expectations, traders said.
Very few companies sold junk bonds on Wednesday, although a busy calendar of new deals was slated for the end of the week, players said.

Wednesday's business included USN Communications Inc's sale of $100 million in units which included senior discount notes and warrants. Lead underwriter Merrill Lynch & Co priced the notes (Caa1/B-) to yield 14.625 percent. The units also included warrants to purchase up to 11 percent of the company and an additional five percent, if the company completes an equity offering by September 30, 1998.
New high-grade bond issues on Wednesday included a $300 million offering from Texas Utilities Co and a $125 million transaction from Martin Marietta Materials Inc.
